approaches.name: single procurement portal and budget transparency portal publishing fiscal data
approaches.description: The project builds a single procurement portal publishing plans, tenders and awards plus a budget portal posting reports and answering citizen queries. Practices: Single Procurement Portal for public procurement transparency; Single Procurement Portal publishing procurement plans, notices and awards; Single Procurement Portal as gateway to e-GP adoption; Phased SIFMIS rollout from recording to workflow mode; Budget transparency portal publishing in-year reports and statements; Phased SIFMIS rollout prioritizing highest-payment governorate finance offices; Single Procurement Portal publishing tenders and contract awards; Budget Transparency Portal with Citizen's Budget Helpdesk.

evidence.text: It also supports establishing a Single Procurement Portal (SPP) that will be critical for promoting transparency and providing all necessary information on public procurement to the government, the private sector, and the public.

The SPP will be critical for promoting transparency and providing all necessary information on public procurement to the government, the private sector, and the public.
It is the first step towards the adoption of an e-government procurement system in the future.

The data to be generated from the portal will help the regulatory body assess the performance of the procurement system against a set of indicators and to subsequently adjust procurement policies to achieve the best value for money.

The phased implementation approach will be incremental, starting with the core modules (budget upload, general ledger, revenue recording, expenditure, reporting), and will operate in recording mode during the first phase.

After the core modules are launched in recording mode during the first six months of the system ‘going live’, transaction processing will transition to workflow approval mode with mandatory document attachment and implementation of more modules/functions.

Tools will be prepared to support the upload of in-year budget reports and annual financial statements on government websites/Syria Budget Transparency Portal in user- friendly formats for easy public consumption.

To ensure good coverage of the SIFMIS, eight out of the fifteen Governorate Finance Offices that account for around eighty percent of the value of average payments will be prioritized for the initial SIFMIS rollout - Ministry of Finance (Central Department), Damascus, Damascus Rural, Aleppo, Tartous, Lattakia, Homs, Hama.
A rollout strategy will be developed to achieve full coverage of all governorates in the medium-term.
The web-based SIFMIS will be accessible online by the 14 Governorate Payment Centers and line ministry with total end-users estimated at around 2,000.

approaches.name: integrated SIFMIS with biometric payroll, banking interfaces and secure infrastructure
approaches.description: The project deploys a web-based SIFMIS with biometric payroll, bank interfaces, digital signatures, disaster recovery and blockchain grant tracking. Practices: Web-based PFM e-learning with online testing and self-certification; SIFMIS payroll module with biometric registration; API linking SIFMIS to CBS core banking and SYGS; Digital signature with PKI for secure fiscal transactions; Centralized payroll module with biometric entry/exit controls; SIFMIS core financial management modules for central government entities; Resilient SIFMIS infrastructure with solar backup and tiered data centers; On-premises hot disaster recovery center with real-time SIFMIS replication; blockchain Funds Chain platform tracking grant proceeds; SIFMIS processing of budget payments and payroll; Biometric registration of staff in SIFMIS payroll module.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: online self-certified PFM training modules - cue: 'web-based learning' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The same could be made available for officials from remote areas.

extra_evidence.text: This will be a web-based learning program using the same study material as for the PFM courses as a computer-generated study program with on-line testing at end of each subject with self-certification to complete each module.

The envisaged Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) SIFMIS will support procedural and control systems to ensure the legality, accuracy and timelines of fiscal information in the following core PFM functions: budget preparation, budget execution, human resource/payroll with biometric registration (including robust data protection and privacy safeguards), expenditure control, cash management, purchasing, revenue management, fixed asset registration, inventory management, accounting, reporting, audit trails, and financial reporting/analytics with in-built dashboards for online publication.

The project will support development of an Application Programming Interface (API) or the use of file transfer to exchange data (where API is not technically possible) between the CBS in-house developed core banking system (Nahas) and the in-house Syrian Gross Settlements System (SYGS) for interbank transfers, with the SIFMIS for revenue, expenditure, and automated bank reconciliation.

The project will support adoption of Digital Signature with Public Key Infrastructure (PKI8), which will be fundamental components for secure online communication and 6 https://uptimeinstitute.com/tiers - An individual equipment failure or distribution path interruption will not impact operations.

To address the current fragmented personnel lists that reside in various ministries, the SIFMIS will include a seamlessly integrated centralized payroll module with biometric registration functionalities to enforce system- based entry/exit controls, position controls, grade/scale, location, allowances, etc .
Authority to change personnel records and payroll will be restricted with a digital audit trail to ensure full integrity of personnel/payroll data.

The MoAD will maintain the authority to approve the creation of new positions and manage the civil service register, with each employee being assigned a Unique Personnel Identification Number (UPIN), which will also be used for payroll purposes.
The implementation of the core modules of SIFMIS is assessed as doable within three years since the coverage is limited to ‘public entities of an administrative nature’ within the central government.
The simplified business processes and basic functions provide a good opportunity for bidders to propose a fit-for-purpose solution.
Such a similar approach is expected to deliver quick-wins to improve commitment controls and publish timely and accurate fiscal reports including donor-financed projects.
The project will incorporate energy-efficient infrastructure, tiered data center standards, solar power backup for continuity, and remote access features.
As one of the first initiatives of its kind in Syria’s public sector, it may also help demonstrate the potential for low-emission digital transformation in public administration.
SIFMIS also enables remote online bill submissions ensuring continuity during climate shocks.
In addition to the on- premises PDC at MoF that will have an in-built back-up, to minimize downtime or data loss, there will be a fully active on-premises hot DRC at a different location.

The DRC will have real-time replication of the SIFMIS and underlying data to take over automatically or with minimal manual intervention if the PDC services are unavailable, therefore providing the highest level of resilience11.
SEAFS will utilize Funds Chain (FC), an innovative blockchain-based platform that will be provided by the Bank to facilitate traceability on the use of Grant proceeds during Project implementation.

evidence.text: Drawing from this framework, the project will provide support to design the Syria Budget Transparency Portal -a public budget dashboard to serve diverse types of users, including citizens (The Timor-Leste Transparency Portal12 is a good example).

extra_evidence.text: To enhance fiscal transparency, budget execution reports (BERs) will be published on this dashboard, as well as geo-mapped project outputs with SIFMIS fiscal data when applicable, by leveraging the Geo-Enabling initiative for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS).

To foster citizens’ interest and ownership of the public budget, the dashboard will also incorporate a “citizen’s budget helpdesk” to respond to citizens’ queries and suggestions regarding Syria’s budget .
